correctness.rationale: The seven Laurent characters are distinct modulo q-1 for every q>=5, so the code has dimension seven. A common factor of three or four sections forces a segment or unit-triangle Newton polygon by the exhaustively checked 127-subset convex-hull classification; its residual has respectively four or three monomials. The segment residual is a Segre square, so independent triple sections have at most one off-fiber zero and a full four-dimensional residual space has none. The triangle residual contributes none. With no common factor, two generic members intersect in at most the anticanonical degree six. This proves q>=7; for F5 complete enumeration of all 8008 six-point and 4368 five-point subsets gives minimum evaluation ranks five and four. Explicit fiber-plus-point and fiber-only linear systems attain the bounds. Any three distinct torus evaluation rows are linearly independent via Vandermonde/affine projections, proving the final three weights. All required finite checks were replayed from the actual files.

value.rationale: The complete remaining higher-weight hierarchy of a natural anticanonical toric surface code is a motivated higher-dimensional subcode-support invariant. The sharp q-point versus (q-1)-point base-locus transition distinguishes three-dimensional sections admitting a ruling fiber plus one isolated base point from four-dimensional systems, a geometric refinement not encoded by the known first and second weights. The nontrivial third/fourth weights hold uniformly for every prime power q>=5, with a verified small-field boundary. The final three weights complete the natural finite hierarchy rather than being offered as separate routine increments.
